name: National Museum of FS History (replica)
summary: L-4 lookout replica built in 2005 for a Smithsonian festival in Washington, D.C.; now at ground level on the National Museum of Forest Service History campus near Missoula.
design: L-4 style lookout replica, based on 1930s-era plans
status_note: A 2005 replica, not the original 1930s-era lookout, and not on its first site.
agency: National Museum of Forest Service History, a nonprofit independent of the USDA Forest Service

access.note: Museum campus open seasonally, 10am to 4pm, Memorial Day weekend to the day after Labor Day, seven days a week, per a listing written while the new building was under construction; current hours may differ.

visit.trail_note: Set at ground level in the middle of the Forest Discovery Trail, per a 2020 association report.

events.note: Built by the Forest Service's preservation team for the Smithsonian Folklife Festival on the Mall in Washington, D.C., celebrating the Forest Service centennial, with materials salvaged from Minton Peak Lookout.
A $500 Forest Fire Lookout Association restoration grant, matched by its Montana-North Idaho Chapter, was used for restoration of the lookout on the museum grounds.
